voice_policy: plain modern English, second person, present tense; no promises of results; quotes only from the linked spans (≤ 25 words), shown not spoken

lines.text: Start with three long breaths, thinking bud with the in-breath, and dho with the out.

quote.text: Start out with three or seven long in-and-out breaths

lines.text: Keep the word as long as the breath.
Now simply be clearly aware of each breath, in and out.
Observe the breath. Is it comfortable or not? Broad or narrow? Fast or slow, short or long, warm or cool?
If it doesn’t feel comfortable, adjust it until it does. If long breathing feels wrong, try short.
When the breath feels comfortable, breathe in at the base of the skull and let it flow down the spine.
In at the base of the skull again… down the right leg, to the toes, and out into the air.
Again from the base of the skull: down the spine, down the left leg, out past the toes.
From the base of the skull over both shoulders, down the arms, and out through the fingertips.
From the base of the throat, down the front of the body, all the way to the belly.
Breathe in at the middle of the chest and let it go all the way down to the belly.
Let all these breath sensations connect and flow together.
Explore: in long, out long… in long, out short… in short, out long… in short, out short. Then breathe whichever way is most comfortable.

quote.text: Breathe whichever way is most comfortable for you.

lines.text: Get to know the resting spots of the breath. The tip of the nose.
The middle of the head.
The palate.
The base of the throat.
The breastbone, at the tip of the sternum.
The navel, or just above it.
Now center your awareness on whichever spot feels most comfortable.
Don’t force the breath. Breathe freely and naturally.
Let the mind be at ease with the breath, but not so much that it slips away.
Spread your awareness, your sense of feeling, throughout the entire body.
Let the breath sensations flow together through the whole body. Keep your awareness as broad as you can.

quote.text: keeping your awareness as broad as possible
